title: The Emperor's New Clothes
blurb: Two men sell an emperor a suit made of nothing.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… in a bright little kingdom by the sea, there was an Emperor who loved clothes more than anything in the world.

[amused] He had a coat for every hour. He had shoes he had never worn twice. [playfully] Other kings sat on their thrones and ruled — but THIS Emperor was almost always in front of a mirror.

[mischievously] Now one day, two strangers came to the city. They were not weavers at all. They were thieves. [short pause] But they were very clever thieves.

[softly] “We weave a magic cloth,” they told the Emperor. “The finest in the world. [whispers] But it has one strange quality. It cannot be seen by anyone who is stupid… or unfit for his job.”

[excited] Well! The Emperor gave them gold. He gave them silk. He gave them a room with two great looms in it.

[amused] And the thieves sat down and began to weave… [short pause] nothing at all. Their looms were empty. Their needles held no thread. But their hands moved all day long, back and forth, back and forth.

[curious] After a week, the Emperor sent his oldest, wisest minister to look.

[worried] The old man walked in… [short pause] and saw two empty looms.

[whispers] “I see nothing,” he thought, and his heart went cold. “Am I stupid? Am I unfit for my job? [firmly] I must never let anyone find out.”

[calmly] So he bowed and said, “Magnificent. Truly magnificent.”

[amused] And so it went. Everyone who came to look saw nothing… and everyone said it was beautiful. Because nobody wanted to be the fool.

[grandly] At last the thieves declared the suit was finished. They mimed lifting it. They mimed dressing him. [playfully] The Emperor turned this way and that before the mirror, wearing nothing at all, and said, “Yes. It fits perfectly.”

[excited] Then out he went, into the streets, under a golden canopy, for the whole city to admire.

[amused] And the whole city DID admire it. [short pause] “What colours!” they cried. “What a fit!” Because every single person had heard about the magic cloth, and not one of them wanted to be called a fool.

[softly] And then, from somewhere near the front, a small clear voice said the simplest thing in the world.

[curious] “But he hasn't got anything on.”

[surprised] It was a child. [short pause] And a whisper went through the crowd… and the whisper became a murmur… and the murmur became a roar of laughter.

[gently] The Emperor knew. [amused] But he lifted his chin, and walked all the way home — because sometimes the hardest thing of all is to say you were wrong.
